## Blocker-tag semantics analysis (Step 5c-bis contract preservation)

The two edits that pin blocker tags do so with correct semantics WRT the /issue Step 5c-bis strip set `{marker-shape, smoke-run-missing, git-provenance}`:

- **Edit A (Step 4 pin FAIL):** A real `ruff-policy` pin failure is a genuine lint violation — the same class as any other substantive code defect the reviewer catches. Correctly pinned as `substantive` (NOT strippable). The prose spells the rationale out explicitly: "the pin failure is a real lint violation, not a marker formatting issue, so it is NOT strippable by /issue Step 5c-bis". This is consistent with Rule 8 (mechanical-contract objections never stand alone) and Rule 12 (blocker grounding). A future reviewer FAILing on a real pin failure will produce a blocker that survives the Step 5c-bis strip, forcing an implementer round instead of a silent pass-through.

- **Edit D (Step 0.5 missing-(c)-field FAIL):** An absent (c) field is a marker-presentation issue — the same class as an absent smoke-section or a missing gate-scope line. Correctly pinned as `marker-shape` (STRIPPABLE per Step 5c-bis). The prose explicitly notes: "The `marker-shape` tag remains strippable by /issue Step 5c-bis (`code-reviewer.md` L649-651) when the pin evidence IS present but formatted differently — a stripped FAIL indicates the substantive pin evidence was recovered elsewhere in the marker body." This is the correct graceful-failure design: a formatting-only mismatch on PRESENT evidence never bounces a round (preserves the #1701 shape, plan Risk d), while a genuinely-missing (c) field still triggers a marker-shape FAIL that the orchestrator surfaces for re-post.

The two-tag split cleanly separates SUBSTANCE (real pin failure → never stripped) from PRESENTATION (missing field on present evidence → strippable). No Step 5c-bis contract contradiction; the strip set stays `{marker-shape, smoke-run-missing, git-provenance}` unchanged.
